2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that Khuku Rani, mother of present respondent No.1, as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 33 of 1990 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Dumuria, Khulna for declaration of her title in .39 acre of land stating, inter alia, that 63 decimals of land was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 182 of Mouza Bhadradia under Police station Dumuria, District Khulna, in the name of Krishnalal Karmakar in 10 annas share and Priyanath Karmakar in 6 annas share who were in amicable possession thereof under owner Surjakanta Sarker and others. Krishnalal died leaving his only wife Hemanta Dashi and, thereafter, Hemanta died leaving her only daughter, the plaintiff. The plaintiff looked after the suit property being .39 acre as the reversioner; that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit land as its owner and there are fruit bearing tress and the plaintiff possessed the suit land by collecting fruits and cultivating crops in the vacant portions; that the plaintiff and her predecessors have been possessing the suit land for more than sixty years. After the death of Priyanath, his son Mohadeb was in possession and enjoyed his share and after the death of Mohadeb, his son defendant No. 2, Prafullah Karmakar was possessing and enjoying the same. At the initial stage the suit land was recorded in the name of the plaintiff in S.A. Khatian, but afterwards the same was wrongly recorded in name of defendant No. 1 without any basis and it was beyond the knowledge of the plaintiff. The plaintiff was under an impression that, like her other lands, the suit land was also recorded in her name and she was in possession and enjoying the same as her own, On 02.04.1990 the local Tashilder claimed that the suit land was Government Khas land and disclosed that he had sent a proposal for settlement of the same to some persons. After enquiry on behalf of the plaintiff, her son Joydeb (present respondent) came to know that a proposal was sent for settlement of the said 63 decimals of land in the name of some persons in Settlement Case No. 1/88-90 and in order to deprive the plaintiff, defendant No. 2 was trying to take settlement in his name and hence the suit. 

 3. Defendants Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing separate written statements. The case of defendant No. 1 was that the suit land was correctly recorded in the S.A. Khatian No. 1 in the name of defendant No. 1 and was under the supervision of the Government. Subsequently, a proposal   was sent to the higher authority for approval of settlement of the suit land to landless Jabbar and another in settlement Case No. 01 of 1989-90. That the plaintiff and defendant No. 2 had never any right, title and possession in the suit land; that the plaintiff is not a legal successor of Krishnalal Karmakar and that the plaintiff collusively filed the suit to grab the suit land on false assertion and, therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Defendant No. 2 contested the suit denying the material facts made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that during continuance of the right, title and possession of Krishnalal Karmakar having 10 annas share and Priyanath Karmakar having 6 annas share, one Manager for the Syedpur Trust Estate purchased their shares in auction for failure to pay Government rent and took possession after giving proper notice to them. On 30.01.1954 defendant No. 2 took settlement of 63 decimals of land from Syedpur Trust Estate when the said land was proposed for giving settlement and on the same day the defendant No. 2 executed a kabuliyat in favour of the owner who accepted the kabuliyat and since then defendant No. 2 has been possessing the suit land by obtaining Dakhilas on payment of rent. At first the record of said .63 acre of land was prepared in the name of defendant No. 2, but later the same was wrongly recorded and published in the S.A. Khatian No. 1 in the name of the Government. The eldest son of defendant No. 2 Arabinda has been residing in the suit land by erecting dwelling but thereon and that the plaintiff has no right, title and possession in the suit land in any side. Hence, the instant suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 13. Although, the judgment of the High Court Division appears to be equally abrupt as the judgment of the lower appellate Court, we find from the judgment of the trial Court that proper discussion was made of the evidence and materials on record. However, it appears that there is a discrepancy in the description of the boundaries as mentioned in the schedule to the plaint and those stated by P.W.1 in evidence. In that respect, we are of the view that the trial Court was wrong in declaring title of the plaintiff in a specific portion of the suit land. The trial Court observed that the plaintiff claimed to be the only heir of Krishna Lal which was not denied by the defendants and as such he was entitled to 39 out of 63 decimals of the suit land by inheritance. On the other hand, defendant No. 1 was not able to substantiate as to on what basis the whole of the land was recorded in the khas khatian. It was further observed that defendant No. 2 could not produce any evidence with regard to the auction sale by which the suit land was purchased by Syedpur Trust Estate. The trial Court also noticed that the Exhibit-'ga' and 'ga-1' was tampered and no witness was called by defendant No. 2 in support of his claim to have taken settlement from the original owner. Accordingly the trial Court did not believe the claim of defendant No. 2.
